about: 50 issues and pull requests written for this sample, of invented projects: no text from a real repository, no real person's name or handle, no address. Each record is a state as the GitHub source writes it: `body` null for an issue with no description, `labels` the label names sorted one a line, `changed_files` empty for an issue and, for a pull request, the number of files it changes and their paths. Each record carries the answer a maintainer would give to each question from the record alone: yes, no or unsure for a yes-or-no question, and for kind the name of one of its options, or unsure. "unsure" means that maintainer would not decide from the record alone and would send it to review. A live run counts agreement this way. For kind, an option agrees when the model's top option is that option at confidence 0.50 or above, and unsure agrees when the confidence is below 0.50. For missing_reproduction, unsure agrees with a probability strictly between 0.30 and 0.70; for not_priority, strictly between 0.20 and 0.80; yes and no agree with an automatic yes and an automatic no. The evidence reports a review on a labelled record, and an automatic answer on an unsure record, apart from the answers that are wrong. missing_reproduction is no on every record that reports no bug, every pull request included, as its criteria say, so most of its no answers come from records that are no bug at all and its figure over the whole sample can pass while real bug reports go wrong: the evidence reports its agreement on the records labelled bug_report apart from the whole, held to the same share. The criteria describe kinds of situations and share no distinctive phrase with any record.

issues.title: Build fails when a page title contains a colon
issues.body:
Version 3.4.2, Ubuntu 24.04, Node 22.

Expected: the site builds.
Actual: the build stops with `FrontMatterError: unexpected token ':' at line 1` and exits with code 1.

Putting the title in quotes works around it.

issues.title: Signed out on every click since upgrading to 2.0 behind a reverse proxy
issues.body:
Since going from 1.9.3 to 2.0.0, signing in works and then the next click sends me back to the sign-in page.

Setup: Docker image 2.0.0 behind nginx, which terminates TLS and forwards plain HTTP to the app.

Steps: sign in, open any note, and you are on the sign-in page again.

The session cookie now carries the Secure flag, and I think the app drops it because it sees plain HTTP from the proxy. Going back to 1.9.3 fixes it.
